newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P ASSIGNS AA+ RATING TO MUNICIPALITY. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S&P ASSIGNS AA+ RATING TO MUNICIPALITY. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's on Monday affirmed an AA+ rating with a stable outlook to Finland's Municipality Finance Ltd's 1.5 billion Finnish markka medium-term note programme.

"Standard & Poor's assigns a 'AA+' rating with a stable outlook to Municipality Finance Ltd.'s Finnish markka 1,500 million MTN programme, and to the two Finnish markka 300 million bonds maturing in 1999 and 2001, respectively, issued under the MTN programme," it said.

In a separate statement, Municipality Finance (Kuntarahoitus Oy) and lead manager Postipankki said Kuntarahoitus was setting up a programme to issue up to 1.5 billion markka worth of bonds, with the first due to be launched on December 11.
The bonds are guaranteed by the Municipal Guarantee Board (corrects from "the local Government Pensions Institution").
One of the 300 million markka bonds will have a 3.75 percent coupon and mature in September 1999, the other, maturing in September 2001, will have a 4.60 percent coupon.
S&P said Municipality Finance benefitted from "strong asset quality with lending purely to the municipal sector."
"Finland's local governments have successfully met the increasing challenges posed by high unemployment and lower state grants," S&P said.
